:::{#exr-ols-slope-r}
#### OLS slope and the correlation

Assuming $S_{xx} > 0$ and $S_{yy} > 0$ (@def-centered-sums),
write the OLS slope $\hcoef{x}$ from @thm-ols-slr
in terms of the
[Pearson correlation coefficient](exploratory-descriptive.qmd#def-pearson-r) $r$
and the
[sample standard deviations](exploratory-descriptive.qmd#def-sample-sd)
$s_x$ and $s_y$ of the $x_i$ and the $y_i$.
:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

::::{.solution}

In terms of the centered sums (@def-centered-sums),

$$
r = \frac{S_{xy}}{\sqrt{S_{xx} S_{yy}}},
\qquad
s_x = \sqrt{\frac{S_{xx}}{n-1}},
\qquad
s_y = \sqrt{\frac{S_{yy}}{n-1}}.
$$

So:

$$
\begin{aligned}
r \, \frac{s_y}{s_x}
&= \frac{S_{xy}}{\sqrt{S_{xx} S_{yy}}} \cdot
  \frac{\sqrt{S_{yy} / (n-1)}}{\sqrt{S_{xx} / (n-1)}}
&& \text{(substitute $r$, $s_x$, $s_y$)}\\
&= \frac{S_{xy}}{\sqrt{S_{xx}} \sqrt{S_{yy}}} \cdot
  \frac{\sqrt{S_{yy}}}{\sqrt{S_{xx}}}
&& \text{(cancel the factors of $n - 1$)}\\
&= \frac{S_{xy}}{S_{xx}}
&& \text{(cancel $\sqrt{S_{yy}}$)}\\
&= \hcoef{x}
&& \text{(closed-form OLS slope)}
\end{aligned}
$$

::::
